This is a suit filed by the plaintiff claiming damages of Rs. 1,75,000/- with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of the suit till the date of payment against the defendants.

2. The case of the plaintiff in brief is as under:-
The plaintiff is the owner in possession of the suit schedule property.
He has purchased the same through registered sale deed dtd: 8.5.1995.
Since from the date of purchase he is in possession and enjoyment of the suit property.
The katha has been changed to his name.
He has been paying taxes to the suit property till this date.

When the defendants interfered with his possession and denied his title to the suit property, the plaintiff filed suit in O.S.No.5686/2015 before the City Civil Court,
Subramanya Bhat K vs Nanjamma on 5 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87355125/
2 Bengaluru for declaration of his title and for possession and it is pending.
During the pendency of the said suit, on 6.5.2016 the defendants and other supporters came near the suit property and damaged the building constructed by the plaintiff in it.
In respect of the said incident, the plaintiff's brother Maha baleshwar Bhat has given a complaint to Rajarajeshwari Nagar police station.
After investigation the police have filed charge- sheet and criminal case is registered in C.C.No.27409/2016 against defendant No.2 and his supporters.
The plaintiff has spent a sum of Rs. 1,50,000/- to repair the said building and at the time of demolition of the said building, the defendants have taken away bag which containing Rs. 25,000/-.
Therefore, the plaintiff is entitled to recover damages of Rs.1,75,000/- from the defendants with interest.
Hence this suit.
3. The defendants No. 1 and 2 have filed written statement.
They have contended that the suit is not maintainable.

It is contended that defendant No.1 is the owner of Sy.No. 212 measuring 5 Acres 16 guntas of land situated at Halage wadarahalli village, Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk, having purchased the same from Smt. Sarasamma under a registered sale deed dtd: 10.10.1984 and 2 nd defendant is the owner of Sy.No. 213 measuring 5 acres 30 guntas of land situated in the same village having purchased the same from Smt. Chikka Thayamma through a registered sale deed dtd:
10.10.1984.
The plaintiff is claiming that he has purchased the suit property from Vishwabharathi House Building Co-operative Society Ltd., through a registered sale deed dtd: 8.5.1995.

entities.text: Vishwabharathi House Building Co-operative Society Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: But the vendor of the plaintiff was not the owner of the either Sy.No. 212 measuring 5 acres 16 guntas or Sy.No. 213 measuring 5 acres 30 guntas situated at Halagewaderahalli village.
Therefore, they could not form any sites and sell the same in favour of the plaintiff.

The plaintiff is well aware of the litigation faced by the Vishwabharathi House Building Co-operative Society Ltd., and he is also aware that the society has failed to establish its title in respect of the above said lands.

entities.text: Vishwabharathi House Building Co-operative Society Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The said society has failed in all legal proceedings up to the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
Therefore, just to harass defendants No.1 and 2, society has instigated the plaintiff to file this false suit.
It is denied that plaintiff has put up a building in the suit property.
The above said lands remained as agricultural lands till this date, no conversion order has been obtained.
As such the question of formation of sites does not arise.
The plaintiff by bribing the Rajarajeshwari Nagar police manged to file charge-sheet against the defendant No.2.

It is denied that the plaintiff has spent a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- to repair the building and the defendants No.1 and 2 have snatched a bag containing Rs.25,000/- from the plaintiffs brother K. Mahabaleshwar Bhat.
The SLP Civil No. 20309- 20310/2015 filed by the above said society was pending before the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India as on 6.5.2016 and present plaintiff was also a respondent in it.
There was an order to maintain status-quo, which was in operation as on 6.5.2016.
The plaintiff has not stated the survey number in which the suit schedule property has been carved out.
The plaintiff has filed this suit by making false allegations.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of the suit.

On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, the following issues have been framed :-
1.
Whether the plaintiff proves that defendants have trespassed into the suit schedule property and have caused damage to the suit schedule property to the tune of Rs.1,75,000/- ?
2. What reliefs plaintiff is entitled ?
5. To prove his case, the plaintiff himself has been examined as PW-1 and got marked 23 documents as Ex. P-1 to P-23.
The SPA holder of the defendant No. 3 is examined as DW-1 and got marked 23 documents as Ex. D-1 to D-23.
6. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for plaintiff, and the arguments of learned counsel for defendant No.3.
He has filed Memo of citations.
1. (1991) 2SCC 141 (Gokak Patel Volkart Ltd., V. Dundayya Gurushiddaiah Hiremath and Ors.)

7. My answer to the above issues are as under:
Issues No.1 : In the Negative, Issue No. 2 : As per final order, for the following :-
REASONS 8. Issue No. 1:- The plaintiff has been examined as PW-1.
He has reiterated the plaint averments in his evidence.
Ex . P-1
is the certified copy of the registered sale deed dtd: 8.5.1995 executed by Vishwabharathi House Building Co-operative Society Ltd., in favour of plaintiff in respect of the suit property.

entities.text: Vishwabharathi House Building Co-operative Society Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Ex . P-2
is the certified copy of the possession certificate issued by the said society to the plaintiff in respect of the suit property.

Ex.P-3 is the certified copy of the katha endorsement dtd:
4.12.1998 issued by the Pattanagere City Municipal Council in favour of plaintiff in respect of the suit property stating that the katha of the suit property has been registered in the name of the plaintiff.

Ex.P-4 is the certified copy of the encumbrance certificate which depicts the sale of the suit property by the society of plaintiff as per Ex.P-1 Sale deed.
9.
The above documents produced by the plaintiff prima- facie show that the suit property has been purchased by the plaintiff from the said society.
However, the defendants have disputed the same.

It is the contention of the defendants that Sy.No. 212 measuring 5 acres 16 guntas was purchased by the defendant No.1 through registered sale deed dtd: 10.10.1984 from Smt. Sarasamma and defendant No.2 has purchased the Sy.No. 213 measuring 5 acres 30 guntas from Smt. Chikka Thayamma through registered Sale deed dtd: 10.10.1984.

It is their contention that the above said lands were not acquired for the society and therefore, they could not have formed sites in it and sell Subramanya Bhat K vs Nanjamma on 5 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87355125/
4 the same to the plaintiff.
It is their contention that the society has failed to prove its contention in all the legal proceedings up to Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.

From the written statement of defendants, it appears that their contention is that the suit property claimed by the plaintiff comes within the above said lands and the plaintiff has not acquired right in the suit property.
10. DW-1 has produced certain documents.
Ex.D-6 is the certified copy of the judgment in RFA No.1351/2009 connected with RFA No.16/2010.

These two appeals were filed against the judgment and decree in O.S.No. 8934/1996 on the file of V Addl. City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru decreeing the suit for the relief of permanent injunction.

entities.text: V Addl. City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It was a suit filed by the Vishwabharathi House Building Co-operative Society restraining the defendants therein from interfering with the possession of the society in respect of Sy.No. 12/2 measuring 5 acres 16 guntas and Sy.No. 213 measuring 5 acres 30 guntas of Halagevaderahalli.

In the said suit, it was asserted by the society that the owners of said land i.e., Sarasamma and Chikka Thayamma had executed agreement of sale dtd:
12.1.1984 and other documents such as affidavits, GPA etc., and delivered possession of the above said lands.
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka allowed the appeals and dismissed the suit filed by the society for permanent injunction.
Ex.D-7 is the certified copy of the order of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Spl. Leave to Appeal in No.20309-20310/2015.
It is an interim order dtd: 27.7.2015 wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court directed the parties to maintain status-quo as regards possession, nature of property and title.
It is to be noted that the said Spl. Leave to Appeal were filed against the judgment and decree passed in RFA No. 1351/2009 and 46/2010 dtd: 9.3.2015.

Therefore, from this order it is clear that Hon'ble Supreme court has directed the parties to maintain status-quo in respect of possession, title and nature of the property i.e., Sy.No.212 measuring 5 acres 12 guntas and Sy.No.213 measuring 5 acres 30 guntas.
There is no much dispute that the suit property is one of the sites carved out in the above said lands.
11. As per the documents produced by the plaintiff, he had purchased the suit property on 8.5.1995 itself from the above said society.
12. In the chief examination of Pw-1, he has stated that he has put up a small house in the suit property in the year 2002 and enclosed the same with barbed wire fence.
It is the contention of the plaintiff that the defendants have demolished the said house on 6.5.2015.
According to the plaintiff this suit is for claiming damages in respect of demolition of the said house.

13. On going through the above said judgments, passed in RFA No.1351/2009 and 46/2010 dtd:
9.3.2015 the society has failed to prove its possession over the above said lands.
Under such circumstances, the society forming sites in those lands in the year 1995, transferring the title and handing over the possession of one of the sites to the plaintiff, is not probable.
It is to be noted that both parties have not produced the subsequent orders of the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
Therefore, till the final decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, it cannot be said that the plaintiff has acquired right, title and interest over the suit property.

It is to be noted that in the judgment in the above said RFA the Hon'ble High court has observed that the suit property being vacant land it is settle position of law that plaintiff can establish possession only on the basis of title deeds, which the plaintiff admittedly, did not possess and hence, the suit ought to have ben dismissed.
Therefore, the Hon'ble High Court has observed that society has not produced title deeds to prove their possession.

Subramanya Bhat K vs Nanjamma on 5 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87355125/
5 14.
PW-1 has stated in his evidence that the revenue documents in respect of Sy.No. 212 are still in the name of the defendant No.1.
It appears that the dispute regarding right, title, interest and possession of suit property has not been decided finally.

15. The contention of the plaintiff is that during the pendency of the suit in O.S.No.5786/2015, the defendants herein and their supporters came near the suit property and damaged the building which was existing therein on 6.5.2016.
It is also alleged that on the same day the defendants have taken away the bag of K. Mahabaleshwar Bhat, which contained cash of Rs.25,000/- belonging to the plaintiff.
The plaintiff has produced a complaint dtd: 6.5.2016 registered on 12.5.2016 in respect of the said incident and it is marked as Ex.P-19.
In the complaint and FIR, names of three persons i.e., Manjunath, Lenkappa and Shashikanth are mentioned as persons who committed trespass and demolition.

Though in the plaint it has been clearly stated that the defendants and their supports came near the suit property and demolished the building and took away the money, the name of the defendants No.1 and 3 is not mentioned in the FIR or complaint only the name of defendant No.2 Lenkappa is mentioned in the FIR and complaint.
In the cause title of the plaint, the age of defendant No.2 is stated as 79 years.
Therefore, at the time of incident, he was aged 76 years.
It is difficult to accept the contention that defendant No.2 came to the suit property and committed the acts alleged by the plaintiff.
16. The plaintiff has produced some photographs to show the act of demolition by the defendants and their supporters.
Ex.P-14 and 15 are those photographs.
By looking into those photographs, it cannot be made out that the shed existing from the year 2002 was demolished in the year 2016.
It appears from Ex.P-14 and P-15 photographs, that a newly put up shed has been demolished.
The cement stones used for the shed appears to be new and it does not appear to be about 14 years old stones.
Therefore, it is difficult to accept the contention of plaintiff that on 6.5.2016, the shed has been demolished by the defendants.

17. In respect of the incident, PW-1 has admitted that defendant No.3 lodged a complaint to the police on 13.5.2016 alleging that plaintiff has trespassed into Sy.No. 212 and 213 by violating the order of Hon'ble Supreme court and filed another complaint on 26.5.2016 alleged trespass into the suit property.
Therefore the allegation of tresspass has been made by the defendants also.

18. DW-1 has stated in his evidence that the acquisition of land in favour of the society has been quashed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka and society has got returned the amount deposited by the government for the purpose of acquisition of said lands.
But the defendants have not produced any document in respect of the same.
19. The plaintiff has contended that for reconstruction of the house in the suit property, he has spent Rs. 1,50,000/-.

To prove the same he has produced receipts issued by PW-3 Venkatesh K as per EX.
P-6 and P-7.
PW-3 has given his evidence before the court.

In the chief examination, PW-3 has stated that on 6.5.2016 at around 6.30 a.m. when he went to the suit schedule property to repair the said house along with labours and Mahabaleshwar Bhat, at 7 a.m., Lenkappa, Shashikanth and Manjunath and their supporters came and threatened them and damaged the fencing, demolished a portion of the building, forcibly taken away the bag of K. Mahabalashwar Bhat.

Further, he has Subramanya Bhat K vs Nanjamma on 5 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87355125/
6 stated that he received a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- from the plaintiff to repair the said building.
But in the cross-examination, PW-3 has stated that he has done the building repair work in the suit property in the year 2002.
Further he has stated that on 22.5.2016, he issued receipt for having received advance amount to construct a new house and after 22.5.2016, he constructed a new house in the suit property.
The evidence of Pw-3 is not consistent with the case of the plaintiff.
20. PW-2 has stated in his evidence that he has taken a sum of Rs. 25,000/- to the suit property to disburse the wages to the coolie workers and on that day 5 workers worked in the suit property.
But Pw-2 has not stated what was the work being done by the daily wage workers on that day.
21. Though the incident has taken place on 6.5.2016, the complaint has been registered on 12.5.2016.

PW-2 has stated that though he went to lodge complaint on 6.5.2016 itself, the police did not receive his complaint as they asked his brother to come, but there is nothing to show that PW-2 has visited the police station on the same day to lodge complaint.

22. Considering the evidence available on record, it is not sufficient to prove that the defendants have damaged the shed put up in the suit property and they have taken away a bag of Pw-2 containing Rs.25,000/- and thereby caused loss of Rs.1,75,000/- to the plaintiff.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Negative.

23. Issue No. 2 :- In view of above discussions, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The suit of the plaintiff is hereby dismissed.
Under the circumstance, the parties shall bear their own costs.
Draw decree accordingly.
